author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Repair CUE track references after renaming a PS2 CD working copy
summary: Preserve the master cue/bin set, audit every FILE entry and track order, update only a disposable working cue, verify unchanged BIN hashes, and test data plus audio before rescanning EmuCoreX.
heroAlt: Brasero optical-disc project showing the image-writing controls used with CD-style multi-track media

blocks.text: The cue sheet is a map, not the audio data

A PS2 CD dump can contain a text cue sheet plus one or more binary tracks. The cue records filenames, track types, and index positions. Renaming BIN files without changing corresponding FILE entries breaks the map; editing track indexes to guess a fix can damage timing. Work only on a copied set and preserve every master hash.
Change filenames and matching FILE references only. Do not alter TRACK mode, INDEX values, pregaps, or track order unless a verified dump log proves the master itself is wrong.

items: Untouched cue/bin master with recorded SHA-256 for each component.
A complete copied working set in an empty folder.
A plain-text editor that preserves encoding and line endings.
The intended portable filenames written before editing.
One repeatable gameplay point and one scene with CD audio for validation.

blocks.text: Reconcile filenames one FILE line at a time

items: 1. Open the working cue as plain text and list every FILE value in order.
2. Compare each value character for character with files in the working folder, including extension and case.
3. Rename one BIN track, then update only its corresponding quoted FILE value.
4. Repeat for remaining tracks while preserving TRACK and INDEX lines exactly.
5. Save the working cue and re-open it to ensure the editor did not add a .txt extension.
6. Calculate SHA-256 for all BIN files and confirm they still match the preservation master.
7. Cold-boot through the working cue, reach gameplay, and play a known music section.
8. Refresh EmuCoreX only after data loading and audio both pass.

blocks.text: If the cue uses one BIN with several TRACK sections, only one FILE value may exist. If it uses several BIN files, every referenced filename must be present. Absolute computer paths make the set non-portable; keep relative filenames and store the cue beside its tracks.
Validate structure, bytes, and audible result
A successful edit changes the working filenames and cue text while leaving all binary track data untouched.

items: Every FILE value resolves inside the same working folder.
No unreferenced BIN track was accidentally left behind.
All binary SHA-256 values equal the master values.
The game cold-boots through the cue.
A known CD-audio segment plays with the expected music and timing.
Emulator cannot find track: filename, extension, quotation, or case differs.
Game boots but music is absent: audio tracks or indexes are not represented as in the master.
BIN hash changed: an editor or conversion touched binary data; discard the working set.
Cue opens as cue.txt: the operating system hid the added extension.

blocks.text: Replace the working set from the frozen master

Delete the disposable working copy only after confirming the master folder, restore the entire cue/bin set into a new workspace, and repeat the rename with the ledger. Do not attempt to reverse guessed INDEX edits line by line.
Case behavior changes across storage systems

Windows often resolves case differences that Linux, Android providers, or network storage may reject. Match cue references exactly and test after the set reaches its real Android destination rather than only on the preparation computer.
